Because the capture engine already has the current accessibility tree in memory, the context injection is free.
extractableIdeas.soWhatTest: The user starts invoking the twin DURING work ('draft a reply to this email', 'what did this person tell me last week?') instead of context-switching to a chat window — turning the twin from a destination into an ambient layer, which is where daily-active usage comes from.

extractableIdeas.idea: Battery-aware processing tiers: on AC power run the full pipeline (OCR fallback, embedding, fact extraction); on battery, capture-and-queue only — defer OCR/embedding/LLM work until plugged in or idle; never software-encode video; keep keyframe JPEGs not video chunks
extractableIdeas.why: Kevin Chen's Rewind teardown prescribes exactly this (defer OCR on battery, hardware encode, kill PNG intermediates), and screenpipe's FAQ confirms local heavy models are the #1 drain with cloud/deferred processing as the documented mitigation. Since TwinMe's memory stream is async anyway (observations batch into reflections), nothing about the product requires real-time processing of every frame.
extractableIdeas.soWhatTest: The user's laptop battery indicator never points the finger at the app (macOS literally names energy hogs in the battery menu) — staying off that list is a hard retention requirement for an always-on app.

extractableIdeas.idea: Local embedding + local search index: fastembed-rs (ONNX, in-process Rust) or EmbeddingGemma-class model embedding captured facts into local SQLite, so on-device search works offline and the cloud memory stream receives only curated, fact-level entries rather than the full firehose
extractableIdeas.why: Keeps the privacy story coherent (search your whole screen history without uploading it), cuts cloud embedding/storage cost to near zero for the 95% of captures that never become memories, and matches the existing TwinMe pattern where the cloud memory stream stores importance-scored observations, not raw data. EmbeddingGemma runs in <200MB RAM quantized; fastembed-rs drops into the Tauri Rust process directly.
extractableIdeas.soWhatTest: The user searches 'that pricing page I saw Tuesday' and gets an instant local hit even offline — while their cloud twin memory stays small, cheap, and composed only of things actually worth remembering.

extractableIdeas.idea: Encryption at rest from day 1 using the OS keystore (macOS Keychain-wrapped key for the SQLite DB and frame store; DPAPI/TPM on Windows), and explicit opt-in for capture at onboarding
extractableIdeas.why: This is the Recall lesson paid for in public: shipping unencrypted local capture nearly killed the feature and forced a ground-up rebuild (VBS enclaves, TPM keys, Windows Hello, opt-in). Rewind's teardown flagged the identical gap. Security researchers now treat 'screen recorder with plaintext SQLite' as a standing target — it WILL be audited.
extractableIdeas.soWhatTest: When (not if) a researcher or journalist points sqlite3 at the app's data directory, they find ciphertext — and the resulting story is 'this one does it right', which for a personal-AI capture product is marketing you cannot buy.

internal.summary: TwinMe Desktop is a shipped, auto-updating Tauri 2 app (v0.2.15, ~10MB) with three real capabilities: (1) an ambient capture engine — a 5s foreground-window poll (macOS Accessibility incl. bounded in-window TEXT extraction; Windows/Linux title-only; no screenshots, no OCR, no keystrokes) writing "clips" and heuristic meeting sessions to local SQLite, synced every 2 min to /api/observations/clip|meeting where they become user_memories observations (source=desktop_clip imp 4 / desktop_meeting imp 5 — the 299 desktop* memories); (2) a polished 10-step native onboarding with two earned wow moments (LLM narration of 75s of live activity via /api/desktop/observe-summary, and zero-LLM extracted facts from Google Calendar via /api/desktop/extracted-facts) plus mid-flow system-browser Google sign-in landing tokens in the OS keyring; (3) a Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+T always-on-top Hummingbird panel that loads the remote /widget chat (full twin-chat SSE pipeline). Tray menu, local settings window, rotating-refresh-token keyring auth, minisign-signed silent auto-update, and 4-target CI release flow all work. The glaring gap vs an ambient assistant: the data flows one way. Capture goes up; nothing proactive ever comes down — the notification plugin is used only for update notices, proactive_insights never reach the desktop, the panel chat is context-blind to the very clips the app captures, the "briefing cards" screen is explicitly fictional, and the LLM action pills are rendered as non-interactive spans because "the chat surface doesn't exist on the desktop yet". The new product is largely a wiring job between assets that already exist.

findings.claim: Capture = 5s foreground-app poll, text-only, never screen recording or OCR
findings.detail: clip_indexer.rs polls every 5s (POLL_INTERVAL=5s). active_window.rs implements per-OS focused-window detection: macOS via AXUIElementCreateSystemWide (app name + window title), Windows via GetForegroundWindow + GetWindowTextW + QueryFullProcessImageNameW, Linux via X11 _NET_ACTIVE_WINDOW (Wayland returns None). macOS ONLY additionally extracts text inside the focused window via a bounded AX-tree walk (MAX_DEPTH 8, MAX_NODES 500, MAX_BYTES 8000), captured exactly once at clip-open with a TOCTOU re-check against the exclude list. Windows/Linux clips carry title only (content stays NULL). No screenshots, no OCR, no audio, no keystroke capture anywhere.

findings.claim: Local store: SQLite clips.db with privacy controls baked in
findings.detail: clips.rs creates clips / excluded_apps / app_settings / meetings tables at the OS data dir (e.g. %APPDATA%/TwinMe/clips.db). Pause flag persisted in app_settings (tray + settings toggle, indexer checks each tick). Per-app exclude list checked BEFORE insert — excluded apps never produce a clip. Tray offers Exclude-current-app and a live Excluded-apps re-include submenu.

findings.claim: Meeting detection (Phase 5A) is window-title heuristics, no audio
findings.detail: meetings.rs classify_meeting() matches Zoom / Microsoft Teams / Webex / FaceTime / Slack (title contains 'huddle') / browser-based Google Meet (title keying). Indexer opens a session when a meeting window is focused, closes on next non-meeting focus. Sessions <60s are noise-filtered locally (never posted). Phase 5B (Whisper transcription, true call presence via audio) is explicitly NOT built — cpal is a dependency used solely to trigger the OS mic-permission prompt during onboarding (audio_permission.rs records nothing).
findings.source: desktop/src-tauri/src/meetings.rs; desktop/src-tauri/src/sync.rs (MIN_MEETING_MS); desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs request_mic_permission; desktop/README.md Phase 5A/5B

findings.claim: Sync: 2-min batched HTTPS upload; clips become user_memories observations (the 299 desktop* memories)
findings.detail: sync.rs posts ≤50 unsynced ended clips to https://www.twinme.me/api/observations/clip and meetings to /api/observations/meeting (canonical www host is regression-tested because the apex 307-redirect strips the Authorization header). Backend observations-clip.js validates per-clip (coercion so one bad clip never poisons the batch), then addMemory(userId, summary, 'observation', {source:'desktop_clip', app, window, started_at, ended_at}, importance 4, skipImportance) — content-bearing clips store the extracted text (≤8000 chars), title-only clips store 'Opened {app} — {title}'. observations-meeting.js stores '45-min Zoom meeting — Standup' at importance 5, source 'desktop_meeting'. addMemory dedups identical content within 24h making retries idempotent. platformStateService.js (line 178-187) surfaces the desktop as a connected 'mirror' platform via metadata->>source LIKE 'desktop%'.

findings.claim: Onboarding v2 is a 10-step native HTML flow with two real-data wow moments
findings.detail: www/index.html (2279 lines, flag twinme_desktop_onboarded_v9): 0 welcome (right-rail dashboard mock, live name binding), 1 name, 2 context permission (un-pauses indexer via settings_set_paused), 3 mic permission (cpal TCC prompt), 4 hotkey demo (split-screen with an animated Hummingbird panel mock over a fake app window), 5 75s 'use your computer normally' observe countdown (skippable after ~SKIP_AFTER_MS), 6 mid-flow Google sign-in, 7 reveal 'Here's what I noticed' — demo_get_clips (deduped-by-app recent clips, TwinMe itself filtered out) POSTed to /api/desktop/observe-summary, 8 'Here's what I learned about you' extracted-facts wow screen (requires the step-6 JWT; skipped entirely if sign-in skipped), 9 fictional 'Tomorrow your twin surfaces things like this' briefing-card grid (work/travel/family/finance/social/content, AskJo-style; trust line says 'These are examples'). Fact rows are inline-editable + dismissable, but edits persist to localStorage only — the ingestion endpoint is an acknowledged follow-up.

findings.claim: Wow moment 1 backend: observe-summary narrates titles with an honesty-constrained LLM
findings.detail: POST /api/desktop/observe-summary is UNAUTHENTICATED BY DESIGN (body is the only input, nothing touches the DB; global rate limiter only). TIER_ANALYSIS (DeepSeek) with a prompt that demands verbatim proper nouns from window titles, forbids inventing specifics or implying screen reading, and returns strict JSON {summary, insight, actions[≤2, ≤8 words]}. The action pills are rendered as non-interactive <span>s with an explicit code comment: 'no chat surface to dispatch into... wire up when the post-sign-in chat handoff is built'.

findings.claim: Wow moment 2 backend: extracted-facts is zero-LLM, pure computation over Google data
findings.detail: POST /api/desktop/extracted-facts (authenticated): single Google Calendar fetch (primary calendar, 30 days, ≤250 events) + OAuth userinfo, then 5 pure fact builders — identity (email domain → company), location (timezone → city), calendar cadence (dominant weekdays + %), recurring focus blocks (titles appearing ≥2x), language signal (non-English Unicode in titles, verbatim examples). Ranked by confidence, capped at 6, Redis-cached 1h per user. Target p50 <600ms, zero LLM calls. Fallback reasons (no_calendar_connected/oauth_expired) drive a connect-calendar CTA in the UI.

findings.claim: Hummingbird quick panel = global hotkey + always-on-top window loading the remote /widget chat
findings.detail: Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+T toggles a 460x600 frameless, transparent, always-on-top, skip-taskbar window whose URL is https://twinme.me/widget?panel=1 (tauri.conf.json) — i.e. the React Widget.tsx page: a chrome-less twin chat reusing the FULL streaming pipeline POST /api/chat/message?stream=1 (memory retrieval, personality, the works), text-only (action/proposal SSE events deliberately ignored). Blur or Esc dismisses (Esc invokes hide_hummingbird, granted by capabilities/twinme-panel.json to that window+origin only). It shares the main window's session and self-heals if summoned pre-login. www/hummingbird.html is a local action-launcher variant (Talk to twin / Soul signature / Open full app buttons) that the window config does NOT load — a bundled stub superseded by the remote /widget. Critically, the panel receives NO context about the user's current activity — the capture engine and the chat never meet on-device.
findings.source: desktop/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json windows[1]; src/pages/Widget.tsx; desktop/www/hummingbird.html; desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs show_hummingbird

findings.claim: Auth: OS-keyring rotating-refresh-token architecture, fully solved for the desktop
findings.detail: Access JWT (~30min) + 128-hex refresh token live in the OS keyring (macOS Keychain / Windows Credential Manager / Linux keyutils), migrated from the legacy auth.toml. The remote twinme.me page pushes tokens via store_auth_token/store_refresh_token IPC commands, scoped by capabilities/twinme-auth-bridge.json to exactly: main window, https://twinme.me + subdomains, those 3 commands, no core APIs. Refresh is body-based POST /api/auth/refresh with client=mobile (because WebView2 drops the sameSite=Strict cookie on twinme:// navigations), serialized by a process-wide Mutex since refresh tokens rotate on use; the refresh token never leaves Rust. Sign-in runs in the SYSTEM browser (Google blocks webview OAuth): open_external (Rust-validated to twinme.me URLs only) → /desktop-handoff page mints a one-time code (POST /auth/desktop-handoff, provider 'desktop_handoff' in auth-simple.js:1791) → twinme://auth?auth_code=... deep link → handle_deep_link either dispatches a CustomEvent into the bundled onboarding page (mid-flow) or forwards to /oauth/callback (post-onboarding). Sync does one-shot 401→refresh→retry.
findings.source: desktop/src-tauri/src/auth_refresh.rs; desktop/src-tauri/src/config.rs; desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs (store_auth_token, handle_deep_link, open_external); desktop/src-tauri/capabilities/twinme-auth-bridge.json; src/pages/DesktopHandoff.tsx

findings.claim: Auto-updater + release flow are live; binaries are unsigned (no Apple/Authenticode certs)
findings.detail: tauri-plugin-updater checks GitHub latest.json (stefanogebara/twin-me releases) once at startup from Rust (remote page can never trigger it), verifies minisign signature, downloads + installs silently, applies next launch, fires a native notification. CI (.github/workflows/desktop-build.yml) builds 4 targets (macOS arm64 + x86_64 cross-compiled on macos-14, Windows x64, Linux x64), runs cargo test on Linux, and tauri-action publishes a GitHub Release with merged latest.json on desktop-v* tags. App-level code signing is still absent — Gatekeeper/SmartScreen warnings documented on /download; the updater minisign signature is separate and IS configured. api/routes/desktop-download.js is a closed same-origin proxy fixing Brave's GUID-filename bug. Current version 0.2.15.

findings.claim: Settings surface is thin and partially stale
findings.detail: Native settings window (www/settings.html, tray-invoked): pause-capture toggle, excluded-apps list with Remove, account-connected pill, hotkey label (display only — not rebindable, despite lib.rs comment 'user can rebind later from settings'), and a HARDCODED version '0.1.6' while the app is at 0.2.15. Onboarding copy promises 'delete everything anytime in Settings' (index.html step 2) but no deletion control exists in settings.html — only pause/exclude.

findings.claim: Gap: zero proactive delivery — the ambient loop is one-way
findings.detail: tauri-plugin-notification is registered and the README claims 'native notifications proxied from TwinMe's web push', but the ONLY notification ever fired is the updater's 'TwinMe updated' notice. proactive_insights, briefing cards, nudges, goal celebrations — all exist server-side but nothing pushes them to the desktop; there is no polling loop, no push channel, no insight surface. Step 9's briefing cards are explicitly fictional. The Hummingbird mock shows a 'Summarize what I'm reading' suggestion that the real /widget cannot do (it gets no clip context). The action pills from observe-summary are display-only.
findings.source: grep notification across desktop/src-tauri/src (only update.rs:45 fires one); desktop/www/index.html steps 4+9; src/pages/Widget.tsx (context: {platforms: []})

findings.claim: Gap: no local intelligence; raw window text leaves the machine; clips are unaggregated
findings.detail: All summarization is server-side. macOS clips upload up to 8000 chars of raw in-window text per focus change; one user_memories row per (app,window) focus change at fixed importance 4 with skipImportance — no on-device sessionization, batching into activity blocks, or local LLM. Memory-stream composition note in CLAUDE.md says platform_data/observations are already sparse vs reflections, but high-frequency clip ingestion can flood the observation stream. Known code debt: macOS AX refs leak one retain per 5s poll (TODO in active_window.rs:65).

findings.claim: Gap: platform coverage asymmetry
findings.detail: In-window content extraction is macOS-only (Windows/Linux clips are app+title only — and a past bug where Windows nulls were silently dropped is documented in the clip schema comment, now fixed with .nullish()). Wayland yields nothing at all. Meeting detection inherits the same blindness: it cannot distinguish 'app focused' from 'actually in a call' without the unbuilt 5B audio work.

extractableIdeas.idea: The capture engine is a finished ambient sensor — build on it, not around it
extractableIdeas.why: 5s poll, cross-platform active-window, macOS text extraction, SQLite queue, pause/exclude privacy controls, idempotent batched sync into the memory stream, 401-self-healing auth: this is the hardest 60% of any ambient assistant and it is production-tested (299 real memories landed). The new product's job is to make this data DO something, not to re-capture it.
extractableIdeas.soWhatTest: Any new-product plan that proposes rewriting capture should be rejected; the differentiating work is downstream of clips.db.

extractableIdeas.idea: Hummingbird + clip context = 'a twin that knows what you're doing right now' in one small change
extractableIdeas.why: The always-on-top hotkey panel already runs the full twin-chat pipeline (memory retrieval, personality, SSE streaming). The desktop already knows the current foreground app/title/content (demo_get_clips exists as an IPC command and the panel capability system makes scoped exposure trivial). Passing the last few clips into Widget.tsx's chat context turns a generic chat popup into the product the onboarding mock promises ('Summarize what I'm reading') — the single highest-leverage wire-up in the codebase.
extractableIdeas.soWhatTest: Ship a panel that opens pre-seeded with 'I can see you're in {app} on {title}' and the demo writes itself.

extractableIdeas.idea: The native notification channel is the missing half of the ambient loop, and both ends already exist
extractableIdeas.why: Server-side proactive_insights (with urgency, categories, nudges) are generated continuously; client-side tauri-plugin-notification is registered with allow-notify permission. A modest poll-or-push bridge (e.g. the 2-min sync loop already authenticates every cycle — it could pull undelivered insights on the same tick) converts the desktop from a sensor into an assistant. Step 9's fictional briefing cards are the ready-made product spec for what these notifications/cards should look like.
extractableIdeas.soWhatTest: If a real insight ('Your focus block starts in 2 hours') arrives as a native notification within a week of work, the ambient-assistant pitch is no longer fictional.

extractableIdeas.idea: The onboarding wow-machinery is a daily-brief generator wearing first-run clothes
extractableIdeas.why: observe-summary (LLM narration of activity with verbatim-proper-noun honesty constraints, insight, suggested actions) and extracted-facts (zero-LLM, sub-600ms, cached fact builders over calendar/identity) are both generic pipelines artificially scoped to onboarding. Run observe-summary over a day of clips instead of 75 seconds and you have the morning briefing; run the fact builders on a schedule and you have the always-fresh 'what I know about you' panel. Cost profile is already disciplined (TIER_ANALYSIS / zero-LLM).
extractableIdeas.soWhatTest: Same endpoints, different trigger cadence — no new ML work required for a daily 'here's what your day looked like' surface.

extractableIdeas.idea: Meeting sessions are the wedge for the highest-perceived-value feature
extractableIdeas.why: Session boundaries (platform, title, duration) are already detected, stored, noise-filtered, and synced. Phase 5B (audio + transcription) is the named next step with cpal already a dependency and the mic permission already requested during onboarding — the user consent moment has already happened. Meeting notes are the one ambient feature users pay for on day one (Granola et al. proved the market).
extractableIdeas.soWhatTest: The delta to 'TwinMe took notes in your 45-min Zoom standup' is audio capture + the existing voice-transcription path, not a new product.

extractableIdeas.idea: The auth + updater rails make the desktop the fastest iteration surface TwinMe has
extractableIdeas.why: Keyring session persistence, deep-link OAuth handoff, capability-scoped remote webviews, and silent minisign auto-update on desktop-v* tags mean: most new features ship server-side instantly (the main window and the panel are remote pages), and the rare binary change reaches every install automatically on next launch. There is no app-store review loop anywhere.
extractableIdeas.soWhatTest: A new panel surface or onboarding screen deploys with a Vercel push; treat the Rust shell as stable infrastructure and ship the new product as web surfaces inside it.

extractableIdeas.idea: Honor the privacy promises before scaling capture — they are the brand
extractableIdeas.why: The codebase consistently treats privacy as a feature (text-only capture, exclude-before-insert, TOCTOU re-checks, 'nothing stored until you sign in' copy, capability minimalism), but two promises are currently unbacked: 'delete everything anytime in Settings' has no deletion UI, and macOS uploads raw window text with no local redaction. Closing these (a delete-my-desktop-data control; local secret/PII scrubbing before sync) is cheap now and existential later.
extractableIdeas.soWhatTest: If the new ambient product increases capture surface (audio, more content), the unkept deletion promise becomes a launch-blocking trust gap.

verified.claim: Hotkey overlay assistant pattern: Highlight's Cmd+. window-aware overlay; Cluely's invisibility is a dead end
verified.detail: Highlight AI: Cmd+. (mac) / Ctrl+. (win) summons an overlay over the current app, grounded in on-screen content + local audio transcription, with integrations (GitHub, Notion, Slack, Calendar) — the user never leaves their app. Cluely's 'undetectable' overlay reportedly hooks the GPU rendering pipeline (Metal/DirectX) to draw below the OS capture path because NSWindow.sharingType=.none stopped working against ScreenCaptureKit on macOS 15; detection vendors now use behavioral signals instead, and the open-source clone Pluely (Tauri, ~10MB binary) demonstrates the overlay mechanics in the consumer's exact stack. Building on capture-invisibility is an arms race against the OS vendor — adopt the hotkey+context-grounding pattern, skip the stealth.
verified.note: Core architecture claim confirmed by independent sources. (1) Highlight AI: docs.highlightai.com confirms Cmd+./Ctrl+. overlay assistant with screen content auto-attached, voice input, and GitHub/Notion/Slack/Google Calendar integrations; local meeting transcription confirmed by third-party coverage (TechCrunch, reviews current as of May 2026). (2) macOS 15+ breakage confirmed exactly: Tauri issue #14200 is titled "macOS 15+: ScreenCaptureKit ignores setContentProtection / NSWindow.sharingType" — all NSWindow content is composited into one framebuffer that ScreenCaptureKit captures; Apple Dev Forums (thread 792152) confirm deliberate change, no workaround, no public API; issue labeled upstream-blocked. (3) Pluely confirmed: github.com/iamsrikanthnani/pluely, Tauri, ~10MB, open-source Cluely alternative demonstrating overlay mechanics (its own "undetectable" claim is broken by #14200 on macOS 15+). (4) Behavioral-signal detection confirmed: Fabric (20+ signals: gaze reading-vs-recall patterns, response-timing variance, blink rate), Talview, Kira AI. CAVEAT on one sub-claim: Cluely's GPU-pipeline hook (Metal/DirectX, drawing below capture path) is reported only by third-party reviews; Cluely's own undetectability docs say merely "same privacy technology Zoom employs" with no technical detail, and the best independent teardown (adamsvoboda.net) of the near-identical Interview Coder found ordinary WDA_EXCLUDEFROMCAPTURE / NSWindow.sharingType flags — which QuickTime captured anyway. Keep the "reportedly" hedge; treat the GPU-hook mechanism as unverified marketing, not fact. Strategic conclusion (skip stealth, adopt hotkey+context-grounding) is well-supported: Apple is actively closing capture-invisibility paths and detection vendors bypass rendering tricks entirely via behavioral analysis.
